question: Should OpenClaw commit to this AI-safety taxonomy as a core plugin SDK contract with durable shared-state history and a built-in operator UI, or should the initial capability remain limited to existing diagnostics/plugin seams?
rationale: This choice determines the stable external API, the ownership of sensitive retained telemetry, and the migration/retention policy; those are product and compatibility commitments that code review cannot safely infer.

options.title: Approve a bounded core contract
options.body: Sponsor a narrowly specified event schema, plugin capability, storage retention policy, and operator surface, then require upgrade and real-runtime proof before merge.

options.title: Keep the core generic
options.body: Limit core changes to a generic diagnostics seam and move taxonomy-specific exporters, dashboards, and policy logic into plugins.

options.title: Defer the feature
options.body: Pause this branch until an owner defines the privacy, retention, and plugin-API product contract.

recommendation.title: Approve a bounded core contract
recommendation.body: Sponsor a narrowly specified event schema, plugin capability, storage retention policy, and operator surface, then require upgrade and real-runtime proof before merge.

likelyOwner.reason: They authored the feature proposal and implementation and can supply the requested design rationale, although final direction belongs to a repository owner.
